intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Explore the medieval Old Town Square, watch the famous Astronomical Clock chime on the hour, and wander through Gothic alleyways. Join a guided walking tour to uncover the history of Bohemian kings, Jewish Quarter stories, and stunning Baroque architecture along the Vltava riverfront promenade.

experiences.name: Budapest Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Board a scenic cruise along the Danube River at sunset, passing illuminated landmarks including the Hungarian Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge. Enjoy local Hungarian wine and light snacks while soaking in panoramic waterfront views — the closest Budapest gets to a beachfront atmosphere.

experiences.name: Budapest Széchenyi Thermal Bath Experience
experiences.description: Relax in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, set in a stunning Neo-Baroque building in City Park. Soak in outdoor and indoor mineral-rich pools, enjoy the spa atmosphere, and mingle with locals — a uniquely Hungarian cultural ritual that blends wellness with history.

experiences.name: Prague Local Food Market & Czech Cuisine Tasting
experiences.description: Visit the Náplavka Farmers' Market along the Vltava riverbank and sample authentic Czech street food including trdelník, svíčková (beef sirloin), local cheeses, and craft beers. Chat with local vendors, discover seasonal produce, and enjoy a casual riverside dining experience with views of the water.

experiences.name: Budapest Great Market Hall & Hungarian Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Budapest's culinary soul at the iconic Great Market Hall, a stunning 19th-century iron-and-brick structure. Sample langos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese), Hungarian salami, paprika spices, and chimney cake. A self-guided food tour through the stalls offers an authentic taste of Magyar culture and local life.
experiences.location: Fővám tér, Central Market Hall, Budapest

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at 13:00, clear customs, and take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK (~€2.50), then walk or take tram to your hotel in Staré Město. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed self-guided walking tour of Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) — admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj), the Church of Our Lady before Týn, and soak in the medieval atmosphere. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across Charles Bridge at golden hour for stunning views of Prague Castle across the Vltava River. Watch street musicians and browse the statues. Head back to Old Town for dinner in a local pub (hospoda).

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the hotel after check-in — try a street food stall near Old Town Square for a 'trdelník' pastry or a cheap sandwich (~80–120 CZK).
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33) — a beloved Czech pub with affordable traditional dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings. Budget ~200–280 CZK per person including a Pilsner Urquell draft.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour public transport pass (120 CZK) at the airport — valid on buses, trams, and metro. Prague is very walkable from Staré Město. September weather is mild (15–20°C), bring a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) — take Tram 22 from Náměstí Republiky up to Pohořelec. Explore the castle grounds, St. Vitus Cathedral (exterior free; interior ticket ~250 CZK), Golden Lane (tiny colorful houses), and panoramic views over the city. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — explore the charming baroque streets, Wallenstein Garden (free), and the Church of St. Nicholas. Cross Charles Bridge again on foot heading back toward Old Town. Visit the Kafka Museum area or browse the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside — the cemetery exterior is free to view.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods by tram for a more local, less touristy evening. Visit a local kavárna (café) or wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre style breakfast or grab fresh pastries from a local pekárna (bakery) near the hotel — budget ~60–100 CZK.
meals.lunch: Eat near Malá Strana — try U Hrocha (Thunovská 10), a classic Czech pub with hearty lunches for ~150–200 CZK.
meals.dinner: Restaurace Mlejnice (Kožná 14, Old Town) — rustic Czech restaurant with wooden interiors and affordable traditional meals. Expect ~200–250 CZK per person with a beer.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle area involves a lot of uphill walking — wear comfortable shoes. The castle grounds are free to enter; individual attractions have separate ticket fees. A combined ticket for major interiors costs ~350 CZK.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad — Prague's lesser-known but equally stunning fortress on a hilltop south of the city. Take Metro C to Vyšehrad station. Explore the ramparts, the neo-Gothic Church of St. Peter and Paul (exterior free), the old cemetery with famous Czech graves (Dvořák, Smetana), and enjoy sweeping Vltava River views. Almost entirely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the Municipal House (Obecní dům) — admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior for free. Then explore the Powder Tower (Prašná brána) exterior (~90 CZK to climb). Walk through Celetná Street (the Royal Route) back to Old Town. Browse the Havelské Tržiště market (Havelská Street) for cheap souvenirs and local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a classical music concert — Prague is famous for affordable evening concerts in historic churches. Look for performances at St. Martin in the Wall or Chapel of Mirrors (~400–600 CZK). Alternatively, enjoy a free evening walk along the Vltava riverbank.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry and coffee at Pekárna Ondráš or any local bakery near Old Town (~70–100 CZK).
meals.lunch: Picnic at Vyšehrad — buy supplies from a nearby Albert supermarket (bread, cheese, local cold cuts, beer) for ~100–150 CZK total.
meals.dinner: Pivnice Radegast (Templová 2, Old Town) — a classic Czech beer hall with cheap, filling meals like fried cheese (smažený sýr) or pork knuckle. Budget ~180–250 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is far less crowded than Prague Castle and offers a more authentic, peaceful experience. September evenings can be cool — bring a layer. Check local concert listings at www.pragueconcerts.com for budget options.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning to revisit any Prague highlights or explore Nové Město (New Town) — visit Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí), the National Museum (exterior iconic; entry ~200 CZK), and the Mucha Museum if interested in Art Nouveau (~240 CZK). Alternatively, explore the trendy Vinohrady neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Take a budget bus or train from Prague to Budapest. RegioJet or FlixBus run direct routes (~4.5–6 hours, tickets from €10–20 if booked in advance). Depart Prague around 13:00–14:00 and arrive Budapest by evening. Buses depart from Florenc Bus Station (Metro B or C).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest (~19:00–20:00). Check into your accommodation. Take a short evening walk along the Danube riverbank near the Chain Bridge — the illuminated Parliament Building and Buda Castle are breathtaking at night. Completely free.

meals.breakfast: Final Prague breakfast — try a local café near Old Town for eggs and coffee (~100–150 CZK).
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or grab food at Prague's Florenc Bus Station before departure (~100–150 CZK).
meals.dinner: Arrive in Budapest and grab a quick, affordable dinner near your accommodation — try a lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor for ~800–1200 HUF (~€2–3).

day_by_day.notes: Book RegioJet or FlixBus tickets in advance for the cheapest fares (as low as €10). The bus is comfortable with Wi-Fi. Alternatively, a train via Vienna is scenic but slower and pricier. Exchange some Czech Koruna for Hungarian Forint before or upon arrival — Budapest uses HUF, not Euro.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from Clark Ádám tér (~1200 HUF one way) or walk up for free. Visit the Royal Palace exterior, the Hungarian National Gallery (free on select days), Matthias Church (~2500 HUF entry), and Fisherman's Bastion (exterior free; upper towers ~1000 HUF). Panoramic views of Pest and the Danube are stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to the Pest side. Walk along the Danube Promenade and explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) on Fővám tér — Budapest's largest indoor market. Browse fresh produce, Hungarian paprika, sausages, and handmade goods. Try a kürtőskalács (chimney cake) for ~600 HUF.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (VII District) — visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (exterior free; interior ~4000 HUF), and stroll through the vibrant ruin bar district around Kazinczy Street. Visit Szimpla Kert (the original ruin bar) for a drink — beers from ~700–900 HUF.

meals.breakfast: Find a local pékség (bakery) near your accommodation for fresh pastries and coffee (~500–700 HUF).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Great Market Hall — upstairs stalls serve affordable Hungarian dishes like goulash soup, stuffed cabbage, and lángos (~1500–2000 HUF).
meals.dinner: Kádár Étkezde (Klauzál tér 9, Jewish Quarter) — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian lunch/dinner spot beloved by locals. Traditional dishes like chicken paprikash and bean goulash for ~2000–3000 HUF. Cash only.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is busy at the Great Market Hall — arrive before 11:00 for the best experience. The Jewish Quarter ruin bars are most lively on Friday and Saturday nights. Budapest's public transport (BKK) is affordable — a single ticket is ~450 HUF or buy a 24-hour pass for ~2500 HUF.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — one of Budapest's most iconic landmarks, free to visit. Explore the Millennium Monument and the two flanking museums: the Museum of Fine Arts and the Hall of Art (Műcsarnok) — check for free Sunday entry. Walk through the beautiful City Park (Városliget) and see Vajdahunyad Castle (exterior free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the famous Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Széchenyi fürdő) in City Park — one of Europe's largest thermal bath complexes. Entry ~6000–7000 HUF (weekday rates lower). Bring a swimsuit and towel or rent on-site. A quintessential Budapest experience — chess players, outdoor pools, and steaming thermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Take a free sunset walk along the Danube on the Pest side — the Parliament Building lit up at dusk is magical. Then explore the lively Gozsdu Udvar (Gozsdu Courtyard) in the Jewish Quarter for street food, bars, and local nightlife atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local cukrászda (pastry shop) — try a rétes (Hungarian strudel) with coffee (~600–900 HUF).
meals.lunch: Eat near City Park — Bagolyvár Restaurant or a nearby street food stand. Alternatively, pack a picnic from a nearby SPAR or Aldi supermarket (~1000–1500 HUF).
meals.dinner: Menza (Liszt Ferenc tér 2) — a retro-style Hungarian bistro with affordable traditional dishes and a great atmosphere in one of Budapest's most charming squares. Budget ~3000–4000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Baths can get crowded on Sundays — consider arriving right when it opens (~9:00). Bring flip-flops. The thermal baths are a must-do in Budapest and well worth the entry fee. Towel rental is ~600 HUF, locker included in entry.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings. Book a guided tour in advance (~6000 HUF for non-EU citizens) or admire the stunning Gothic Revival exterior from the Danube bank for free. Visit the nearby Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a deeply moving Holocaust memorial, free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a day trip or explore Óbuda and Margaret Island (Margit-sziget) — a tranquil green island in the middle of the Danube, free to enter. Rent a bike (~1500 HUF/hour) or walk around the island's parks, fountains, open-air theater, and ruins of a medieval Dominican convent. Perfect for a relaxed afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city for a farewell Budapest dinner. Explore the Belváros (Inner City) area and the trendy Ráday Street for restaurant options. Optionally, take a budget Danube evening cruise (~3000–5000 HUF) for illuminated city views — book through local operators at the dock.

meals.breakfast: Try a traditional Hungarian breakfast at a local étkezde (canteen) — scrambled eggs, bread, and coffee for ~800–1200 HUF.
meals.lunch: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (Király utca 55) — a legendary, ultra-cheap Hungarian canteen loved by locals. Full meal with soup, main, and drink for ~1500–2000 HUF. Cash only, arrive early.
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen (Sas utca 3) — a Michelin-recommended but surprisingly affordable wine bar/restaurant with Hungarian small plates. Budget ~4000–6000 HUF for a memorable splurge evening, or opt for a simpler local alternative on Ráday Street for ~2500–3500 HUF.

day_by_day.notes: Margaret Island is accessible by Bus 26 from Nyugati tér or on foot/bike via the Margaret Bridge — no cars allowed on the island. Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at www.latogatokozpont.parlament.hu. Monday is a quieter day at most attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Citadella on Gellért Hill for the best panoramic views of the entire city (free to walk up via paths from Gellért tér, ~30–40 min uphill hike). See the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) up close. On the way down, stop at the Gellért Thermal Baths (exterior is a stunning Art Nouveau building) — optionally take a morning soak (~6000 HUF) as a farewell treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall or Váci Street. Pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Unicum herbal liqueur, or embroidered goods as affordable gifts. Head to your departure point — Budapest has two main train stations (Keleti and Nyugati) and a main bus terminal (Népliget) for onward travel.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Budapest. If flying, Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport is connected by Bus 100E (~900 HUF, ~30 min) from Deák Ferenc tér. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Budapest breakfast — grab a fresh lángos from a street vendor near Gellért tér (~700 HUF) or coffee and pastry from a local café.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the market or city center before departure — try a kürtőskalács, pogácsa (savory scones), or a quick bowl of gulyásleves (goulash soup) from a market stall (~1000–1500 HUF).
meals.dinner: Airport or travel meal — pack snacks from a supermarket to save money during transit (~500–1000 HUF).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport travel and security. Bus 100E runs every 20–30 minutes from Deák Ferenc tér and is the cheapest airport connection. Double-check your accommodation check-out time and arrange luggage storage if needed (most hotels offer this for free).

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) or a mid-range taxi (~500 CZK) to your boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a hotel map.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most), admiring the Baroque statues and views of the Vltava River. Continue into the Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the Church of Our Lady before Týn. Keep the pace relaxed — this is your soft landing into Prague.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the narrow cobblestone lanes of Old Town as the golden-hour light hits the medieval facades. Head to the Josefov (Jewish Quarter) boundary for a short scenic walk, then settle in for dinner at a welcoming local restaurant nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the hotel or a nearby café upon arrival — nothing formal scheduled before landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite near the airport or Old Town upon arrival — try a local bakery like Náměstí Republiky area cafés for an open-faced chlebíček (Czech open sandwich) and a Kofola.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33, Old Town) — a beloved Czech gastropub serving tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell and classic svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce). Mid-range, lively, and authentically Czech. Budget ~400–600 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to adjust faster. Old Town is very walkable from your hotel — almost everything on Day 1 is within a 15-minute walk. Avoid heavy sightseeing today; save energy for the full days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a hearty Czech breakfast, then head to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Book a combined ticket (~350 CZK) covering St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, the Golden Lane, and St. George's Basilica. Arrive by 09:00 to beat the midday crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the complex and enjoy panoramic views over Prague's red rooftops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) district. Wander Nerudova Street lined with Baroque palaces, and stop at the Lennon Wall for photos. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore the Old Town side. Visit the Old Town Hall Tower (climb for rooftop views, ~130 CZK) and spend time in the Old Town Square. Pop into the Mucha Museum (~240 CZK) to discover the Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the atmospheric evening in Old Town. Walk through Celetná Street toward the Municipal House (Obecní dům) to admire its stunning Art Nouveau exterior. Then relax over dinner in a cozy cellar restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy-style breakfast at a local café near your hotel — try eggs, cold cuts, and fresh bread. Budget ~150–200 CZK.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Malá Strana at U Malé Velryby (The Little Whale) — a cozy spot with Czech and international dishes, great value. Budget ~300–450 CZK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mincovna (Old Town Square) — solid Czech cuisine with goulash, roasted duck, and local beers in a historic setting. Budget ~400–600 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is a half-day commitment — wear comfortable shoes. The Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) is a highlight with its tiny colorful medieval houses. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket is recommended for the castle hilltop.

day_by_day.morning: Discover the Josefov — Prague's beautifully preserved Jewish Quarter, one of the most significant in Central Europe. Visit the Jewish Museum complex (~550 CZK combined ticket) including the Old Jewish Cemetery, Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial), Maisel Synagogue, and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods via tram for a taste of local Prague life away from tourists. Visit the Žižkov Television Tower (viewing platform ~250 CZK) — controversial but iconic, with David Černý's crawling baby sculptures. Browse the Jiřího z Poděbrad farmers market (open Saturdays, but the square is lovely any day) and explore the leafy residential streets. Return to center via tram.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is one of Europe's great classical music cities. Check listings at the Municipal House (Smetana Hall) or the Rudolfinum for evening performances. Pre-book tickets online (~500–900 CZK). Afterward, enjoy a nightcap at one of Old Town's wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Café Louvre-style spot — try a Czech palačinky (crepes) with jam and coffee. Budget ~150 CZK.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Žižkov at Pivnice U Sadu — a no-frills Czech pub beloved by locals, serving hearty svíčková and Pilsner. Budget ~250–350 CZK.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (if budget allows for a splurge) or a more mid-range option: Eska (Karlín district) — modern Czech cuisine with seasonal ingredients in an industrial-chic space. Budget ~500–700 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is deeply moving — allow time for reflection at the Pinkas Synagogue, whose walls are inscribed with 80,000 names of Czech Holocaust victims. Book concert tickets at least 1–2 days in advance. Tram lines 5, 9, and 26 connect Old Town to Žižkov easily.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Vyšehrad — the lesser-visited but deeply historic fortress on a cliff above the Vltava. Free to enter the grounds. See the Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, the Vyšehrad Cemetery (resting place of Dvořák, Smetana, and Mucha), and enjoy sweeping river views. Far quieter than Prague Castle. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer day: take the afternoon train from Praha Hlavní Nádraží (Prague Main Station) to Budapest Keleti Station. The RegioJet or Czech Railways train journey takes approximately 6.5–7 hours (depart ~14:00, arrive ~21:00). Book seats in advance online (~€20–35 one way). Enjoy the scenic countryside as you cross into Hungary. Arrive in Budapest and check into your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Budapest Keleti (~21:00). Take the metro (M2 line) or a taxi to your accommodation. After settling in, take a short evening stroll along the Danube embankment near the Chain Bridge — the illuminated Parliament Building and Buda Castle across the river are breathtaking at night. A gentle first impression of Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your Prague hotel before checkout — fuel up for the travel day.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the Manifesto Market food trucks near Náměstí Republiky before heading to the station, or grab a sandwich and Czech snacks at the train station. Budget ~200 CZK.
meals.dinner: Light dinner on the train (RegioJet has a bistro car) or grab a quick bite near Budapest Keleti upon arrival — try a nearby lángos stand (fried dough with sour cream and cheese, ~1,000 HUF) for your first authentic Hungarian street food.

day_by_day.notes: Check train schedules and book in advance at cd.cz or regiojet.com. Keep your Czech koruna for any last-minute Prague purchases — you'll need Hungarian Forint (HUF) in Budapest. ATMs are widely available at Keleti station. September is an excellent travel month — trains are comfortable and not overly crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda side of the city. Take the funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~1,400 HUF return) or walk up to Buda Castle Hill. Visit the Budapest History Museum and the Hungarian National Gallery (combined area pass ~4,000 HUF). Wander the cobblestone streets of the Castle District, stopping at the Fisherman's Bastion (free or ~1,000 HUF for tower access) for the finest panoramic views of the Danube and Parliament. Visit the Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, ~2,500 HUF).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Pest side via the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot. Explore the Grand Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest indoor market. Browse stalls of paprika, lángos, Hungarian salami, Tokaj wines, and folk crafts. This is the perfect place to pick up edible souvenirs. Then stroll along Váci Street and Vörösmarty Square.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — Budapest's ruin bar district. Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (largest in Europe, ~4,500 HUF) if open in the evening, or admire its exterior. Then dive into the famous ruin bar scene — start at Szimpla Kert, the original and most iconic ruin bar, for a drink in its eclectic, art-filled courtyard.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near your accommodation — try a pogácsa (savory scone) and a strong Hungarian espresso. Budget ~1,500–2,000 HUF.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Grand Market Hall upper floor — try lángos with tejföl (sour cream) and sajt (cheese), or a bowl of gulyás (goulash soup). Budget ~2,000–3,000 HUF.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Frici Papa Kifőzdéje — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian canteen beloved by locals serving hearty mains like pörkölt (meat stew) and stuffed cabbage. Incredibly affordable and authentic. Budget ~3,000–4,500 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday at the Grand Market Hall is lively but can be busy — go before noon for the best experience. Ruin bars are busiest Friday–Saturday; Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers market if you want a daytime visit. Wear comfortable shoes — Buda Castle Hill involves significant walking and stairs.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a quintessential Budapest tradition: a thermal bath morning. Head to the Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi fürdő) in City Park — one of the largest and most beautiful in Europe, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque yellow palace. A weekend cabin ticket costs ~8,000–10,000 HUF. Soak in the outdoor pools, try the steam rooms, and embrace the local ritual. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) — stroll past Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior, small museum fee inside), a fairy-tale castle built for the 1896 millennium exhibition. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum, ~3,200 HUF) for a world-class collection of European masters. Walk down Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées — stopping at the Hungarian State Opera House (exterior or book a guided tour ~4,900 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Take a Danube River cruise at sunset — one of the most memorable experiences in Budapest. Several operators (Legenda, Mahart) offer 1-hour evening cruises (~5,000–7,000 HUF) with illuminated views of the Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle. Afterward, explore the upscale Belváros (Inner City) area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at the Szimpla Kert Sunday Farmers Market (opens 09:00) — a wonderful local experience with fresh produce, artisan foods, and coffee. Budget ~2,000 HUF.
meals.lunch: Lunch near City Park at Gundel Restaurant (Budapest's most historic, slightly upscale) for a mid-range set menu, or opt for a nearby café. Budget ~5,000–7,000 HUF for Gundel, or ~3,000 HUF at a bistro.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Borkonyha Winekitchen (near the Basilica) — a Michelin-starred restaurant with an excellent Hungarian wine list and seasonal dishes, but with a surprisingly accessible lunch/dinner menu. Reserve ahead. Budget ~8,000–12,000 HUF per person (a worthy splurge evening).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Danube cruise online in advance, especially for the popular sunset departure (~19:00–20:00 in September). Thermal bath tip: bring flip-flops and a padlock for the locker. Széchenyi is the most social and photogenic of the baths — ideal for first-timers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the most spectacular Neo-Gothic buildings in the world. Book an English guided tour in advance (~8,500 HUF for non-EU citizens) to see the Hungarian Crown Jewels and grand state rooms. Tours run every hour. Afterward, walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) and visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — 60 iron shoes commemorating Jews shot into the river during WWII.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Belváros and Lipótváros districts. Visit St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István-bazilika, ~600 HUF) — Budapest's largest church with a panoramic dome terrace (~1,500 HUF). Then head to the Central Market Hall area or browse the antique shops and galleries along Falk Miksa Street — Budapest's antique row. Visit the Dohány Street Synagogue and Jewish Museum (~4,500 HUF) if not visited earlier.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Budapest — make it special. Head to a rooftop bar for sunset cocktails: 360 Bar atop the Alexandra Bookshop on Andrássy Avenue offers stunning city views (~2,000–3,000 HUF for cocktails). Then enjoy a farewell Hungarian dinner in the Jewish Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most iconic café since 1858. Try a Gerbeaud slice (layered walnut and apricot jam cake) with a cappuccino. Budget ~3,000–4,000 HUF.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kárpátia Restaurant (near the Basilica) — a grand historic restaurant with Hungarian classics like halászlé (fisherman's soup) and chicken paprikash. Beautiful Art Nouveau interior. Budget ~4,000–6,000 HUF.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Mazel Tov — a stunning ruin-bar-meets-restaurant in the Jewish Quarter serving modern Middle Eastern and Hungarian-fusion cuisine in a gorgeous greenhouse-style space. Lively and atmospheric. Budget ~5,000–7,000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at jegymester.hu — they sell out quickly, especially in September. The Shoes on the Danube memorial is most powerful at dusk or dawn — plan accordingly. Keep some HUF for tips and small purchases; many places accept cards but cash is always appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a relaxed final morning. If time allows, visit the Budapest Retro Interactive Museum for a fun look at Hungarian life under communism (~4,500 HUF), or take a final stroll through the Great Synagogue area and the charming Gozsdu Udvar courtyard — a series of interconnected courtyards filled with cafés and boutiques. Pick up last-minute souvenirs: Tokaj wine, Hungarian paprika, Unicum herbal liqueur, or handmade embroidery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport. Take the 100E airport bus from Deák Ferenc tér (~900 HUF, ~30–40 min) or a taxi/Bolt (~6,000–8,000 HUF). Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's greatest cities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of Prague's golden spires, Budapest's thermal baths, and the warmth of Central European hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a neighborhood café — try kürtőskalács (chimney cake) from a street vendor or a proper Hungarian breakfast with eggs, salami, and fresh bread at a local étterem. Budget ~2,000–2,500 HUF.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Gozsdu Udvar or grab airport food — keep it simple given departure logistics. Budget ~3,000–4,000 HUF.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your destination.

day_by_day.notes: Double-check your flight departure time and terminal. Budapest Airport has two terminals (2A and 2B) under one roof. Exchange any remaining HUF before departure (rates at the airport are poor — use up cash at the Gozsdu Udvar market instead). Total trip budget estimate (excluding flights and accommodation): ~€600–900 per person for 8 days covering entry fees, meals, transport, and activities at a mid-range level.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury car service (Mercedes E-Class or similar) to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge, admire the Baroque statues, and soak in your first views of Prague Castle across the Vltava River. Wander through Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the twin-spired Týn Church. Keep the pace relaxed after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric lanes of Josefov (the Jewish Quarter) at dusk as the golden hour light hits the historic synagogues. Then head to dinner at a celebrated Prague fine-dining restaurant nearby.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at Café Savoy (Vítězná 5) — an elegant Art Nouveau café serving refined Czech classics like svíčková and freshly baked pastries, a short taxi ride from Old Town
meals.dinner: Dinner at Field Restaurant (U Milosrdných 12, Staré Město) — a Michelin-starred modern Czech tasting menu showcasing seasonal, locally sourced ingredients in a sophisticated setting

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in guarantee with your boutique hotel in advance. Keep Day 1 light on activities — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm private transfer booking before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex exploration. Begin at 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Hire a private licensed guide for a 2-hour tour covering St. Vitus Cathedral (stunning Gothic interior and royal tombs), the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane. Enjoy panoramic views over the red rooftops of Malá Strana and the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) district. Visit the ornate Baroque St. Nicholas Church, then explore the hidden Wallenstein Garden — a serene formal garden with peacocks and a bronze Hercules fountain. Browse the boutique antique shops and artisan galleries along Nerudova Street.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is world-renowned for its chamber music scene. A performance at the Lobkowicz Palace concert hall or the Estates Theatre (where Mozart himself conducted Don Giovanni) is a quintessential Prague evening. Dress smartly.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or at Café Louvre (Národní 22) — a grand historic café with Art Nouveau interiors, serving eggs, pastries, and excellent coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Coda Restaurant in the Aria Hotel (Tržiště 9, Malá Strana) — rooftop terrace with castle views, refined European cuisine with Czech influences
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Augustine Restaurant (Letenská 12) inside the Augustine Hotel — elegant setting in a restored 13th-century monastery, superb European fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Book private castle guide and concert tickets well in advance — Estates Theatre performances sell out quickly, especially in September. Wear comfortable shoes for the castle cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive Jewish Quarter (Josefov) private tour. Explore the six historic synagogues — Old-New Synagogue (Europe's oldest active synagogue, dating to 1270), Pinkas Synagogue (haunting memorial with 80,000 names of Czech Holocaust victims inscribed on its walls), and the evocative Old Jewish Cemetery with its layered tombstones. A private guide adds essential historical and cultural depth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Municipal House (Obecní dům) — a breathtaking Art Nouveau masterpiece. Take a guided interior tour of the Smetana Hall and ornate private rooms. Afterward, explore the nearby Powder Tower and the Celetná Street luxury boutiques. Stop into the Museum of Decorative Arts if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar with panoramic Old Town views — T-Anker rooftop bar atop the Palladium shopping center offers sweeping vistas over the spires of Staré Město. Then a leisurely dinner in the heart of Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or Eska (Pernerova 49) — a celebrated Prague bakery and restaurant known for sourdough, fermented foods, and creative Czech breakfast plates
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (Haštalská 18, Staré Město) — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering a refined multi-course tasting menu rooted in 19th-century Bohemian cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at V Zátiší (Liliová 1, Staré Město) — a long-standing Prague fine-dining institution with an elegant atmosphere, excellent wine list, and creative Czech-international cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Quarter sites are closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays — September 17 is a Thursday, so all sites should be open. Book La Degustation tasting menu well in advance as seating is limited.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (90 minutes from Prague by private car). Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — a UNESCO-listed chapel decorated with the bones of 40,000–70,000 people, an utterly unique and thought-provoking historical site. Then explore the stunning Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara, one of the finest Gothic churches in Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague by early afternoon. Relax and recharge at your hotel's spa or enjoy a leisurely walk along the Vltava riverbank. Visit the Kampa Island area — a tranquil island in the Vltava with the Kampa Museum of modern Central European art, charming cafés, and riverside gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Premium Czech food and wine experience — book a private wine tasting dinner featuring Moravian wines (Czech Republic's celebrated wine region) paired with elevated Czech cuisine. Alternatively, enjoy a river cruise dinner on the Vltava with illuminated views of Charles Bridge and Prague Castle.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Pivnice Dačický (Rakova 8) — a historic restaurant in a Renaissance house serving traditional Bohemian dishes including roast meats and local dumplings
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard a private luxury Vltava river cruise (companies such as Prague Venice Boats offer premium private charters) with a curated Czech tasting menu and Moravian wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car transfer to Kutná Hora — it's far more comfortable than the train for a luxury trip. Book river dinner cruise in advance, especially on a Friday evening in September.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer day: Prague to Budapest by Regiojet or Railjet premium train (approximately 7 hours) or, for ultimate luxury, arrange a private car transfer or book a short flight (1 hour). If taking the scenic train, depart from Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Station) and enjoy the rolling Central European countryside. Arrive in Budapest by early-to-mid afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your luxury Budapest accommodation (recommended: Four Seasons Gresham Palace or Párisi Udvar Hotel for historic grandeur). Once settled, take a first stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side, admiring the dramatic silhouette of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge. Visit the ornate Széchenyi Chain Bridge up close.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Budapest — explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue, a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard lined with neo-Renaissance mansions, luxury boutiques, and the magnificent Hungarian State Opera House. Take an exterior tour of the Opera House and enjoy dinner in the prestigious V. District.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Prague boutique hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in the dining car on the scenic train journey, or a packed premium picnic prepared by your Prague hotel
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Restaurant (Ráday utca 4) — Hungary's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a sophisticated modern European tasting menu with Hungarian influences

day_by_day.notes: If flying Prague to Budapest, book through Lufthansa, Austrian Airlines, or a private charter. Train is highly recommended for the scenic experience — book premium/first-class seats. Confirm Budapest hotel late check-in if arriving by train.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill. Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) from Clark Ádám Square up to Castle Hill. Visit the magnificent Royal Palace complex, the Hungarian National Gallery (exceptional collection of Hungarian fine art), and the charming medieval streets of the Castle District. Admire Matthias Church with its extraordinary Zsolnay tile roof and the neo-Romanesque Fisherman's Bastion for breathtaking panoramic views over the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Víziváros (Watertown) district below the castle. Visit the Király Thermal Baths — one of Budapest's oldest Turkish baths, dating to the 16th century Ottoman occupation. Indulge in a premium thermal bath experience (book a private cabin for ultimate comfort). Alternatively, visit the world-famous Széchenyi Thermal Baths in City Park for a grander, more atmospheric experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar — 360 Bar atop the Paris Department Store on Andrássy Avenue offers sweeping 360-degree views of the city. Then attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of Europe's most beautiful opera houses, with world-class productions at surprisingly accessible prices.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your luxury Budapest hotel's restaurant — the Four Seasons Gresham or Párisi Udvar both offer exceptional morning spreads
meals.lunch: Lunch at Halászbástya Restaurant (Szentháromság tér 5, Castle Hill) — elevated Hungarian cuisine with unrivaled panoramic Danube views from the Fisherman's Bastion terrace
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Onyx Restaurant (Vörösmarty tér 7-8) — a two Michelin-starred Budapest landmark offering an exquisite Hungarian fine-dining tasting menu in an Art Deco setting

day_by_day.notes: Book opera tickets well in advance — September is peak cultural season in Budapest. Onyx Restaurant requires advance reservation. The thermal bath experience is best enjoyed in the afternoon before the evening cultural program.

day_by_day.morning: Deep dive into Budapest's Jewish heritage and Great Synagogue District. Visit the Dohány Street Synagogue — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world, a stunning Moorish Revival masterpiece. Explore the attached Hungarian Jewish Museum and the moving Holocaust Memorial Garden (the Weeping Willow sculpture by Imre Varga). Then walk through the atmospheric Erzsébetváros (VII District) — the historic Jewish Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's magnificent 1897 iron-and-tile market hall. Browse stalls of Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, foie gras, Mangalica salami, embroidered textiles, and artisan goods. An ideal place for premium souvenir shopping. Afterward, walk along the elegant Váci Street and the Danube Embankment, stopping at the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial.
day_by_day.evening: Ruin bar experience in the Seventh District — Budapest's famous ruin bars are a unique cultural phenomenon. Szimpla Kert is the original and most iconic, set in a crumbling pre-war building transformed into an eclectic, atmospheric bar. Enjoy craft Hungarian beers and pálinka (fruit brandy) in this legendary setting. Then a late dinner at a celebrated Budapest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at New York Café (Erzsébet körút 9-11) — often called the most beautiful café in the world, this gilded 1894 palace café serves an opulent breakfast in a jaw-dropping frescoed interior
meals.lunch: Lunch at Borkonyha Winekitchen (Sas utca 3) — a Michelin-starred restaurant celebrated for its creative modern Hungarian cuisine and exceptional Hungarian wine pairings
meals.dinner: Dinner at Stand Restaurant (Székely Mihály utca 2) — a Michelin-starred modern Hungarian restaurant by celebrated chefs Tamás Széll and Szabina Szulló, showcasing the finest contemporary Hungarian gastronomy

day_by_day.notes: New York Café is extremely popular — book a table for breakfast in advance. The Great Market Hall is open Monday–Saturday; it's best visited before 2 PM on weekdays to avoid crowds. Ruin bars are most atmospheric from 8 PM onwards.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere), a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the Millennium Monument with statues of the Seven Magyar chieftains and Hungarian kings. Walk through the adjacent City Park (Városliget) and admire the fairytale Vajdahunyad Castle reflected in its lake. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts on Heroes' Square if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell luxury spa afternoon at the Széchenyi Thermal Baths — the grandest of Budapest's thermal bath complexes, with its iconic yellow neo-Baroque palace and steaming outdoor pools. A perfect, quintessentially Budapest send-off. Return to your hotel for final packing and check-out.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — arrange a private luxury car transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport. Enjoy one final Hungarian meal before your flight, either at the airport's premium lounge or a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely breakfast at your luxury hotel — savor the last moments of Budapest hospitality
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty tér 7) — Budapest's most iconic and historic café and confectionery, founded in 1858, serving exquisite Hungarian pastries, Dobos torte, and refined café cuisine on the elegant main square
meals.dinner: Early farewell dinner at Babel Budapest (Piarista köz 2) — a Michelin-starred restaurant near the Elizabeth Bridge offering innovative modern Hungarian cuisine, perfect for a celebratory final evening

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the transfer and airport procedures. Confirm private transfer booking the evening before. Consider purchasing premium Hungarian souvenirs: Tokaji Aszú wine, Unicum herbal liqueur, Herend porcelain, or Zsolnay ceramics as lasting memories of the trip.
